settings.description: The title Ghostty will use for the window. Forces the title at all times; Ghostty will ignore set title escape sequences from programs. For a blank title, set to one or more spaces (quoted).
settings.name: Static title for all windows

settings.description: Enable URL matching. URLs are matched on hover with control (Linux) or command (macOS) pressed and open using the default system application. The URL matcher is always lowest priority of any configured links.
settings.name: Automatically link URLs
settings.note: Matching occurs while holding the control (Linux) or command (macOS) key.

settings.description:
Enables or disables title reporting (CSI 21 t). Allows the running program to query the terminal title.

WARNING: This can expose sensitive information at best and enable arbitrary code execution at worst.
settings.name: CSI 21 title reporting
settings.note: This allows running apps to read the terminal title.

settings.description: The size of the scrollback buffer in bytes. This also includes the active screen. When the limit is reached, the oldest lines are removed. Scrollback exists completely in memory. Allocated lazily. Per terminal surface, not for the entire application.
settings.name: Scrollback buffer size (bytes)
settings.note: This buffer exists completely in memory but is allocated lazily.

settings.description:
When to scroll the surface to the bottom. Comma-separated list of options. Prefix with `no-` to disable.

Options:
- `keystroke` - Scroll to bottom when a key is pressed that sends data to the PTY (default: on)
- `output` - Scroll to bottom when new data is displayed (default: off)
settings.name: Scroll to bottom on
settings.note: Comma-separated list. Available values: keystroke, output.

settings.description: The total amount of bytes that can be used for image data (e.g. the Kitty image protocol) per terminal screen. Maximum value is 4,294,967,295 (4GiB). Default is 320MB. If set to zero, all image protocols are disabled. Separate for primary and alternate screens.
settings.name: Image buffer limit (bytes)

settings.description:
The reporting format for OSC sequences that request color information (OSC 4, 10, 11).

- `none` - OSC queries receive no reply
- `8-bit` - Color components returned unscaled (e.g. `rr/gg/bb`)
- `16-bit` - Color components returned scaled (e.g. `rrrr/gggg/bbbb`) (default)
settings.name: OSC color report format

settings.description: String to send when ENQ (0x05) is received from the running command. Defaults to an empty string.
settings.name: Response to ENQ

settings.description: If true, allows the 'KAM' mode (ANSI mode 2) to be used within the terminal. KAM disables keyboard input at the request of the application. Not common and not recommended.
settings.name: VT kam mode allowed
settings.note: If you don't know what this is, don't touch it!

settings.description: Trims trailing whitespace on data that is copied to the clipboard. Only applies to trailing whitespace on lines that have other characters. Completely blank lines always have their whitespace trimmed.
settings.name: Trim trailing space on copy

settings.description: Require confirmation before pasting text that appears unsafe. Helps prevent 'copy/paste attacks' where a user may accidentally execute unsafe commands by pasting text with newlines.
settings.name: Confirm when pasting unsafely

settings.description: If true, bracketed pastes will be considered safe. Bracketed pastes are pastes while the running program has bracketed paste mode enabled.
settings.name: Mark bracketed paste as safe

settings.description:
The color space to use when interpreting terminal colors.

- `srgb` - Interpret colors in the sRGB color space (default).
- `display-p3` - Interpret colors in the Display P3 color space.

Currently only supported on macOS.
settings.name: Window colorspace

settings.description: Horizontal window padding between terminal cells and left/right window borders. Value is in points (scaled for DPI). Can specify two comma-separated values for different left/right padding: `window-padding-x = 2,4`.
settings.name: Horizontal window padding

settings.description: Vertical window padding between terminal cells and top/bottom window borders. Value is in points (scaled for DPI). Can specify two comma-separated values for different top/bottom padding: `window-padding-y = 2,4`.
settings.name: Vertical window padding

settings.description: If true, extra padding from viewport not divisible by cell size is automatically balanced between all four edges. The other `window-padding` options are applied first.
settings.name: Auto-balance window padding
settings.note: Distributes only the leftover space evenly across all four edges. Applied after horizontal/vertical padding, not instead of it.

settings.description:
The color of the padding area of the window.

- `background` - The background color specified in `background`
- `extend` - Extend the background color of the nearest grid cell (with heuristics)
- `extend-always` - Same as `extend` but always extends without applying heuristics
settings.name: Window padding color

settings.description: The opacity level of the background. A value of 1 is fully opaque and 0 is fully transparent. On macOS, background opacity is disabled when in native fullscreen. On macOS, changing this requires restarting Ghostty completely.
settings.name: Background opacity

settings.description: Applies background opacity to cells with an explicit background color set. Normally, `background-opacity` is only applied to the window background. Setting this to true will apply it to all cells regardless of whether they have an explicit background color.
settings.name: Force background opacity on cells.

settings.description:
A theme to use. Can be a built-in theme name, custom theme name, or absolute path to a custom theme file.

To specify different themes for light/dark mode: `light:theme-name,dark:theme-name`.

To see available themes, run `ghostty +list-themes`.
settings.name: Color theme
settings.note: Any colors selected after setting this will overwrite the theme's colors.

settings.description:
Modifies the color used for bold text in the terminal.

- Set to a specific color (`#RRGGBB`) - Always use this color for default bold text. Sets remaining bold colors to `bright`.
- Set to `bright` - Use bright color palette for bold text (replaces deprecated `bold-is-bright`).
- Unset (default) - Use the normal foreground color for bold text.

Note: The previous `bold-is-bright` configuration is deprecated and replaced by `bold-color = bright`.
settings.name: Bold text color
settings.note: Set to bright to use bright palette colors for bold text, or a hex color value. Leave empty to use the default.

settings.description: The opacity level of faint text. A value of 1 is fully opaque and 0 is fully transparent.
settings.name: Faint text opacity

settings.description: The minimum contrast ratio between the foreground and background colors. A value between 1 and 21. A value of 1 allows no contrast (e.g. black on black). Based on the WCAG 2.0 specification. Does not apply to Emoji or images.
settings.name: Minimum contrast

settings.description: Whether to automatically generate the extended 256 color palette (indices 16-255) from the base 16 ANSI colors. Colors explicitly set via `palette` are never overwritten.
settings.name: Auto-generate missing palette colors
settings.note: When enabled, Ghostty will generate missing colors (indices 16-231) based on the first 16.

settings.description: Invert the palette colors generated when `palette-generate` is enabled, so that colors go in reverse order. This allows palette-based applications to work well in both light and dark mode. Has no effect if `palette-generate` is disabled.
settings.name: Harmonious palette generation
settings.note: Inverts generated palette colors. Has no effect if auto-generation is disabled.

settings.description: Background color for the window. Specified as either hex (`#RRGGBB` or `RRGGBB`) or a named X11 color.
settings.name: Background color

settings.description: Foreground color for the window. Specified as either hex (`#RRGGBB` or `RRGGBB`) or a named X11 color.
settings.name: Foreground color

settings.description: Background color for selection. If not set, the selection color is the inverted window background/foreground. Specified as hex or named X11 color. Since 1.2.0, can be set to `cell-foreground` or `cell-background`.
settings.name: Selection background

settings.description: Foreground color for selection. If not set, the selection color is the inverted window background/foreground. Specified as hex or named X11 color. Since 1.2.0, can be set to `cell-foreground` or `cell-background`.
settings.name: Selection foreground

settings.description: Whether to clear selected text when typing. If false, the selected text will not be cleared when typing. Selection can still be manually cleared by clicking once or pressing `escape`.
settings.name: Clear selection on typing

settings.description: Whether to clear selected text after copying. When true, the selection will be automatically cleared after any `copy_to_clipboard` keyboard binding. Does not apply to `copy-on-select` copies.
settings.name: Clear selection on copy

settings.description:
Characters that mark word boundaries during text selection (e.g. double-clicking). When selecting a word, the selection will stop at any of these characters.

Each character becomes a word boundary. The null character (U+0000) is always treated as a boundary.
settings.name: Word selection characters
settings.note: Each character is an individual boundary where selection stops. Not a pattern or regex.

settings.description: Foreground color for non-focused (candidate) search matches. Valid values: hex, named X11 color, `cell-foreground`, or `cell-background`. Default is black.
settings.name: Search match foreground
settings.note: Foreground color for non-focused (candidate) search matches. Also accepts `cell-foreground` or `cell-background`.

settings.description: Background color for non-focused (candidate) search matches. Valid values: hex, named X11 color, `cell-foreground`, or `cell-background`. Default is golden yellow.
settings.name: Search match background
settings.note: Background color for non-focused (candidate) search matches. Defaults to golden yellow (#ffe082). Also accepts `cell-foreground` or `cell-background`.

settings.description: Foreground color for the currently selected (focused) search match. Default is black.
settings.name: Selected match foreground
settings.note: Foreground color for the active/focused search match.

settings.description: Background color for the currently selected (focused) search match. Default is soft peach.
settings.name: Selected match background
settings.note: Background color for the active/focused search match. Defaults to soft peach (#f2a57e).

settings.description: The color of the cursor. If not set, a default will be chosen. Specified as hex or named X11 color. Since 1.2.0, can be set to `cell-foreground` or `cell-background`.
settings.name: Cursor color

settings.description: The color of the text under the cursor. If not set, a default will be chosen. Specified as hex or named X11 color. Since 1.2.0, can be set to `cell-foreground` or `cell-background`.
settings.name: Text color under cursor

settings.description: The opacity level of the cursor. A value of 1 is fully opaque and 0 is fully transparent. A sufficiently small value such as 0.3 may be effectively invisible.
settings.name: Cursor opacity

settings.description:
The style of the cursor. Sets the default style; running programs can override using escape sequences (CSI q). Shell integration will automatically set the cursor to a bar at a prompt (disable via `shell-integration-features = no-cursor`).

Values: `block`, `bar`, `underline`, `block_hollow`
settings.name: Cursor style

settings.description:
Sets the default blinking state of the cursor. If not set (`undefined`/unset), Ghostty will respect DEC Mode 12 (AT&T cursor blink) as an alternate approach to turning blinking on/off. If set to any value, DEC mode 12 will be ignored but DECSCUSR will still be respected.

Values: `true`, `false`, or leave unset (null/undefined) to follow DEC Mode 12.
settings.name: Cursor blink style
settings.note: The default option defers to DEC mode 12 to determine blinking state.

settings.description: Color palette for the 256 color form. Syntax: `N=COLOR` where N is 0-255 and COLOR is an RGB color code (`#AABBCC`) or named X11 color. The palette index can be in decimal, binary (0b), octal (0o), or hexadecimal (0x).
settings.name: Palette

settings.description:
Font size in points. This value can be a non-integer and the nearest integer pixel size will be selected.

Defaults to 13 on macOS and 12 on other platforms.
settings.name: Base font size

settings.description: Draw fonts with a thicker stroke, if supported. Currently only supported on macOS.
settings.name: Thicken fonts
settings.note: This currently only affects macOS.

settings.description: Strength of thickening when `font-thicken` is enabled. Valid values are integers between 0 and 255. 0 does not correspond to no thickening — it corresponds to the lightest available thickening. Has no effect when `font-thicken` is false. macOS only.
settings.name: Thicken strength

settings.description:
Locations to break font shaping into multiple runs. A run is a contiguous segment of text that is shaped together. Breaking runs prevents ligatures from forming across certain points.

Combine values with a comma to set multiple options. Prefix an option with `no-` to disable it.

Available options:
- `cursor` - Break runs under the cursor.
settings.name: Font shaping breaks

settings.description:
Apply a font feature. To enable multiple font features you can repeat this multiple times or use a comma-separated list.

Syntax: `feat`, `+feat`, `-feat`, `feat on`, `feat off`, `feat=1`, `feat=0`.

To disable programming ligatures, use `-calt`. To generally disable most ligatures, use `-calt, -liga, -dlig`.
settings.name: Font ligature settings

settings.description:
Control whether Ghostty should synthesize a style if the requested style is not available in the specified font-family.

Set to `false` or `true` to disable or enable synthetic styles completely. You can enable or disable specific styles using `bold`, `italic`, and `bold-italic` (to enable) or `no-bold`, `no-italic`, and `no-bold-italic` (to disable). Multiple styles can be combined with commas.

Available style keys are: `bold`, `italic`, `bold-italic`.
settings.name: Synthetic styles
settings.note: See the docs for more info.

settings.description:
What color space to use when performing alpha blending. The default is platform-specific: `native` on macOS, `linear-corrected` on all other platforms.

Values:
- `native` - Perform alpha blending in the native color space for the OS (Display P3 on macOS, sRGB on Linux).
- `linear` - Perform alpha blending in linear space.
- `linear-corrected` - Same as `linear`, but with a correction step applied for text that makes it look nearly or completely identical to `native`, but without any of the darkening artifacts.
settings.name: Alpha blending colorspace

settings.description:
The method to use for calculating the cell width of a grapheme cluster.

- `unicode` - Use the Unicode standard (default, correct but may cause cursor-desync with legacy programs).
- `legacy` - Use a legacy method such as wcswidth (maximizes compatibility with legacy programs).

If a running program explicitly enables terminal mode 2027, then `unicode` width will be forced regardless of this configuration.
settings.name: Grapheme width calculation

settings.description:
The font families to use. You can generate the list of valid values using the CLI: `ghostty +list-fonts`.

This configuration can be repeated multiple times to specify preferred fallback fonts when the requested codepoint is not available in the primary font. This is particularly useful for multiple languages, symbolic fonts, etc.

If you want to overwrite a previous set value rather than append a fallback, specify the value as `""` (empty string) to reset the list.
settings.name: Main font family

settings.description: The font family to use for bold text. Falls back to `font-family` if not set or not found.
settings.name: Font family for bold text

settings.description: The font family to use for italic text. Falls back to `font-family` if not set or not found.
settings.name: Font family for italic text

settings.description: The font family to use for bold italic text. Falls back to `font-family` if not set or not found.
settings.name: Font family for bold italic text

settings.description: Force one or a range of Unicode codepoints to map to a specific named font. Syntax: `codepoint=fontname` where codepoint is either a single codepoint (`U+ABCD`) or a range (`U+ABCD-U+DEFG`). Multiple ranges for the same font can be separated by commas.
settings.name: Unicode-specifc font mapping

settings.description: Named font style for the main font. For example for `Iosevka Heavy` use a style of `Heavy`. Set to `false` to completely disable the style.
settings.name: Main font style

settings.description: Named font style for bold text. For example for `Iosevka Heavy` use a style of `Heavy`. Set to `false` to completely disable the style.
settings.name: Font style for bold text

settings.description: Named font style for italic text. Set to `false` to completely disable the style.
settings.name: Font style for italic text

settings.description: Named font style for bold italic text. Set to `false` to completely disable the style.
settings.name: Font style for bold italic text

settings.description: A repeatable configuration to set one or more font variations values for a variable font. Format: `id=value` where `id` is the axis identifier (always 4 characters, e.g. `wght`). Common axes: `wght` (weight), `slnt` (slant), `ital` (italic), `opsz` (optical size), `wdth` (width).
settings.name: Main font variant

settings.description: Variable font variations for bold text. See `font-variation`.
settings.name: Font variant for bold text

settings.description: Variable font variations for italic text. See `font-variation`.
settings.name: Font variant for italic text

settings.description: Variable font variations for bold italic text. See `font-variation`.
settings.name: Font variant for bold italic text

settings.description: Adjust the cell width determined by the font. Values can be integers (1, -1) or a percentage (20%, -15%). Represents the amount to change the original value, not the absolute value.
settings.name: Cell width

settings.description: Adjust the cell height determined by the font. The font will be centered vertically in the cell. Values can be integers or percentages.
settings.name: Cell height

settings.description: Distance in pixels or percentage adjustment from the bottom of the cell to the text baseline. Increase to move baseline UP, decrease to move baseline DOWN.
settings.name: Font baseline

settings.description: Distance in pixels or percentage adjustment from the top of the cell to the top of the underline. Increase to move underline DOWN, decrease to move underline UP.
settings.name: Underline position

settings.description: Thickness in pixels of the underline.
settings.name: Underline thickness

settings.description: Distance in pixels or percentage adjustment from the top of the cell to the top of the strikethrough. Increase to move strikethrough DOWN, decrease to move strikethrough UP.
settings.name: Strikethrough position

settings.description: Thickness in pixels or percentage adjustment of the strikethrough.
settings.name: Strikethrough thickness

settings.description: Distance in pixels or percentage adjustment from the top of the cell to the top of the overline. Increase to move overline DOWN, decrease to move overline UP.
settings.name: Overline position

settings.description: Thickness in pixels or percentage adjustment of the overline.
settings.name: Overline thickness

settings.description: Thickness in pixels or percentage adjustment of the bar cursor and outlined rect cursor.
settings.name: Cursor thickness

settings.description: Thickness in pixels or percentage adjustment of box drawing characters.
settings.name: Box thickness

settings.description: Height in pixels or percentage adjustment of the cursor. Currently applies to all cursor types: bar, rect, and outlined rect.
settings.name: Cursor height

settings.description: Height in pixels or percentage adjustment of maximum height for nerd font icons. Powerline symbols are not affected.
settings.name: Nerd font icon height

settings.description:
Key bindings. Format: `trigger=action`. Duplicate triggers overwrite previous values.

Trigger: `+`-separated list of keys and modifiers (e.g. `ctrl+a`, `ctrl+shift+b`).

Physical keys can be specified using W3C key codes (e.g. `KeyA`, `key_a`).

Special trigger prefix values:
- `all:` - Apply to all terminal surfaces
- `global:` - Make keybind global (system-wide)
- `unconsumed:` - Don't consume the input
- `performable:` - Only consume if action is performable

Special values:
- `keybind=clear` - Clear all keybindings

Chained actions (since 1.3.0): Use `chain=action` as subsequent keybind entries.

Key tables (since 1.3.0): Use `<table>/<binding>` syntax.
Enables the ability to move the cursor at prompts by using alt+click (Linux) or option+click (macOS). Requires shell integration (OSC 133) and only works in primary screen mode.
settings.name: Enable click to move cursor

settings.description: Hide the mouse immediately when typing. The mouse becomes visible again when it is used (button, movement, etc.).
settings.name: Hide mouse while typing

settings.description: Enable or disable mouse reporting. When false, mouse events will not be reported to terminal applications even if they request it. Can be toggled at runtime using the `toggle_mouse_reporting` keybind action.
settings.name: Allow mouse reporting
settings.note: Allows terminal applications to receive mouse events.

settings.description:
Determines whether running programs can detect the shift key pressed with a mouse click. Typically, shift extends mouse selection.

- `false` - Shift not sent with mouse protocol, will extend selection. Program can override with XTSHIFTESCAPE.
- `true` - Shift sent with mouse protocol. Program can override with XTSHIFTESCAPE.
- `never` - Same as false but program cannot override with XTSHIFTESCAPE.
- `always` - Same as true but program cannot override with XTSHIFTESCAPE.
settings.name: Allow shift with mouse click

settings.description:
Multiplier for scrolling distance with the mouse wheel. Can be prefixed with `precision:` or `discrete:` to set the multiplier only for specific device types, comma-separated. If no prefix is used, the multiplier applies to all devices.

Default is 3 for discrete devices and 1 for precision devices. Value will be clamped to [0.01, 10000].
settings.name: Mouse scroll multiplier

settings.description:
The action to take when the user right-clicks on the terminal surface.

- `context-menu` - Show the context menu (default)
- `paste` - Paste from clipboard
- `copy` - Copy selected text
- `copy-or-paste` - Copy if there's a selection, paste otherwise
- `ignore` - Do nothing
settings.name: Right-click action

settings.description:
The action to take when the user middle-clicks on the terminal surface.

- `primary-paste` - Paste from the selection (or system) clipboard per `copy-on-select` (default)
- `ignore` - Do nothing, ignore the middle click
settings.name: Middle-click action

settings.description: The time in milliseconds between clicks to consider a click a repeat (double, triple, etc.). A value of zero uses a platform-specific default (macOS: OS settings, other: 500ms).
settings.name: Milliseconds between multi-click
settings.note: A value of 0 means to use the operating system's default timing.

settings.description:
Changes the behavior of the macOS option key to act as alt.

Default (unset) depends on keyboard layout: `true` for U.S. Standard/International layouts, `false` otherwise.

- `true` - Option treated as Alt (breaks Unicode input sequences)
- `false` - Restore macOS Alt key unicode sequences (breaks terminal Alt sequences)
- `left` - Enable only for left Option key
- `right` - Enable only for right Option key
settings.name: Use option key as alt key
